GET /api/hub/context.description: The hub's identity and state before any session: hub_id, cloud_base_url, language, currency, whether a machine is registered and, only for a live session or a device the PIN door trusts (hub#2510), the PIN users — anybody else gets an empty list. First request of every visit.

POST /api/auth/cloud.description: Send the SaaS user's JWT (`Authorization: Bearer {{access_token}}` — what the SaaS collection's Login saved). The hub verifies it (RS256), links or provisions the local user and opens a session. The response's `token` is saved as `hub_session`.

POST /api/auth/set-pin.name: Set (or change) my PIN
POST /api/auth/set-pin.description: Sets the PIN of the session's user — SIX digits. `current_pin` is required when the user already has one (hub#1430); omit it right after the first cloud login.

POST /api/auth/pin.name: Open a session with name + PIN (the till's day-to-day login)
POST /api/auth/pin.description: Local login. The response's `token` is saved as `hub_session`. `device_id` identifies the client: the device-trust gate refuses a login that does not identify its device (`device_unidentified`).

GET /api/keys.name: API keys of the hub (without secrets)

GET /api/hub/operations.name: Which commands and queries THIS hub accepts — read this before the two doors below
GET /api/hub/operations.description: The dispatcher's own catalogue: every operation `POST /api/query` and `POST /api/command` take a `name` for, with its `kind`, `module`, the `permission` it checks, `payload` (the raw JSON Schema, or null) and `list` (search/sort/filters/page_size of a list query). Internal commands and deactivated modules are NOT listed — the dispatcher would refuse them. `?module=<id>` narrows to one module, `?module=hub` is the core namespace; an unknown module answers an empty list. Needs an ADMIN session; a request that names a module (`X-Erplora-Module`) also needs `manage_flows`.

POST /api/query.name: Run a declarative query of a module
POST /api/query.description: `name` is `<module>.<query>` as declared in the module's manifest — take it from `GET /api/hub/operations`; `params` are its bound parameters. Answers `{ok, data: rows}`. Needs a hub SESSION of any kind (cloud, PIN or badge) — the API key does NOT open this door: it only opens `/api/v1/{module}/q|c/…` and `/webhook`.

POST /api/command.name: Run a declarative command of a module
POST /api/command.description: `name` is `<module>.<command>` — take it from `GET /api/hub/operations`; `payload` follows the command's JSON Schema (the `payload` field of that catalogue). Answers `{ok, data}` or `{ok: false, error: {code, message}}`. Needs a hub SESSION of any kind (cloud, PIN or badge) — the API key does NOT open this door: it only opens `/api/v1/{module}/q|c/…` and `/webhook`.

GET /api/v1/openapi.json.name: OpenAPI of THIS hub's modules — import it into Postman
GET /api/v1/openapi.json.description: The `expose_api` operations of the modules installed on this hub (`/api/v1/{module}/q|c/…`), as OpenAPI 3.1. Per hub: install a module and the API grows. Needs the setting `api_docs_enabled` = true (404 otherwise) and a user session. Import the response into Postman and use `Authorization: Bearer {{hub_api_key}}` on the imported requests.

GET /api/blueprints/catalog.name: Blueprint catalogue (proxied from the SaaS)
GET /api/blueprints/catalog.description: The blueprints published in the marketplace, by sector. Needed once, to pick the one the bench is built from.

GET /api/blueprints/:slug/download.name: Download a catalogue blueprint (zip)
GET /api/blueprints/:slug/download.description: The `*.blueprint.zip` of `slug`. Save it and feed it to POST /api/hub/import/inspect.

POST /api/hub/import/inspect.name: Inspect a blueprint zip before importing (binary body)
POST /api/hub/import/inspect.description: Body = the zip bytes (`application/octet-stream`, pick the file in Postman). Validates it and stages it: the response's `upload_id` goes into POST /api/hub/import.

POST /api/hub/import.name: Import a staged blueprint (migrate-style)
POST /api/hub/import.description: `upload_id` from inspect; `selection` chooses what to apply; `origin` (catalogue slug + version) makes a partial import retryable. Missing modules are installed from the marketplace best-effort; fiscal material lands as `pending`.

POST /api/hub/export.name: Export THIS hub as a blueprint zip
POST /api/hub/export.description: The bench's identity for recreation: everything selected, as a `*.blueprint.zip`. `settings_items` narrows the settings keys (never widens them, ADR-0195).

POST /api/hub/flows/whatsapp-header-imag.name: Upload the photo a flow step sends in a WhatsApp template header
POST /api/hub/flows/whatsapp-header-imag.description: A WhatsApp template approved with a photo header sends a photo on every message, and Meta downloads it from a link. Send the photo as the multipart field `file`: the hub keeps it in its own files (`whatsapp/headers/`, named by the SHA-256 of its bytes) and answers `201 {ref, mime_type, size}`. Put that `ref` in the step's `vars.header_image`; every send asks erplora.com for a freshly signed link to it, so the file never has to be public and the link never expires in the queue. Only a JPEG or a PNG (told by its bytes, never by its name) of up to 5 MB, Meta's cap for a header image. Refusals come back as a code: `whatsapp.invalid_header_image_upload` (not a multipart form), `whatsapp.header_image_missing` (no `file` field), `whatsapp.header_image_unsupported` (415), `whatsapp.header_image_too_large` (413), `whatsapp.header_image_not_saved` (502, erplora.com could not store it). A module reaching this door through `@erplora/module-sdk` (`erplora.forModule(id).flows.uploadWhatsappHeaderImage(file)`) also needs the `manage_flows` capability, declared and granted by the owner; without it the answer is `403 capability_denied`. The shell names no module and is unaffected.

POST /api/hub/whatsapp/template-header-s.name: Upload the sample of a photo, video or PDF template header to Meta
POST /api/hub/whatsapp/template-header-s.description: Meta registers a template whose header is a file only with an example of that file already uploaded to it. Send the file as the multipart field `file`; the hub relays the form in streaming to the SaaS, which uploads it with the business's Meta token and answers `201 {header_handle, format, mime_type, size}`. Register the template with `header_format` (`IMAGE`, `VIDEO` or `DOCUMENT`, the `format` answered here) and `header_handle`, and upload again on every edit. The kind is decided by the file's bytes: JPEG/PNG up to 5 MB, MP4 up to 16 MB, PDF up to 100 MB. Refusals come back as a code: `whatsapp.invalid_header_sample_upload` (not a multipart form with its boundary), `whatsapp.header_sample_length_required` (no `Content-Length`), `header_sample_too_large`, `missing_file`, `unsupported_header_sample`, `no_whatsapp_number`, `whatsapp_not_configured`, `meta_permission_denied`, `meta_rate_limited`, `meta_unreachable`, `meta_template_failed`. A module reaching this door through `@erplora/module-sdk` (`erplora.forModule(id).whatsappTemplates.uploadHeaderSample(file)`) also needs the `notify` capability, declared in its `module.json` with the `whatsapp` channel and granted by the owner in Settings → Permissions; without either the answer is `403 capability_denied`. The shell names no module and is unaffected.

GET /api/hub/whatsapp/templates.name: WhatsApp templates — what Meta says about each one
GET /api/hub/whatsapp/templates.description: This hub's templates with the verdict Meta gave each one (`APPROVED`, `PENDING`, `REJECTED` + `rejected_reason`). `stale: true` means the SaaS could not reach Meta and is answering with what it had stored. Read it when the tab opens, never on a timer: every call refreshes against Meta and that path has no throttle. A module reaching this door through `@erplora/module-sdk` (`erplora.forModule(id).whatsappTemplates`) also needs the `notify` capability, declared in its `module.json` with the `whatsapp` channel and granted by the owner in Settings → Permissions; without either the answer is `403 capability_denied`. The shell names no module and is unaffected.

POST /api/hub/whatsapp/templates.name: Send a template to Meta for review (or edit the one already there)
POST /api/hub/whatsapp/templates.description: Registers the template in the business's Meta account. `201` = new to Meta, `200` = edited in place; either way it goes back to `PENDING`, because Meta reviews an edit again. Refusals come back as a code, never as prose: `invalid_name`, `invalid_category`, `invalid_language`, `missing_body`, `invalid_placeholders`, `invalid_header_placeholders`, `missing_example`, `invalid_variables`, `no_whatsapp_number`, `meta_permission_denied`, `meta_rate_limited`, `meta_unreachable`, `meta_template_failed`. `body` numbers its placeholders `{{1}}…{{n}}` without gaps and `variables` carries one example per placeholder. A module reaching this door through `@erplora/module-sdk` (`erplora.forModule(id).whatsappTemplates`) also needs the `notify` capability, declared in its `module.json` with the `whatsapp` channel and granted by the owner in Settings → Permissions; without either the answer is `403 capability_denied`. The shell names no module and is unaffected.

DELETE /api/hub/whatsapp/templates/:name.name: Delete a template from Meta
DELETE /api/hub/whatsapp/templates/:name.description: Drops the template from Meta and from the SaaS — every language of it, as Meta does. `204` on success; a name this hub does not have is a `404` whether it belongs to another business or to nobody. The name is lowercase letters, digits and underscores: anything else the hub refuses before calling. A module reaching this door through `@erplora/module-sdk` (`erplora.forModule(id).whatsappTemplates`) also needs the `notify` capability, declared in its `module.json` with the `whatsapp` channel and granted by the owner in Settings → Permissions; without either the answer is `403 capability_denied`. The shell names no module and is unaffected.

PATCH /api/business/certificate.name: Use my own certificate — switch on or off (keeps the .p12)
PATCH /api/business/certificate.description: «Usar mi propio certificado». `false` keeps the uploaded .p12 but stops filing with it: the hub files through ERPlora's Sello (the delegated route). `true` files with the own certificate again. Refusals travel as 409 with a stable code: `fiscal.own_certificate_not_uploaded` (on with nothing uploaded), `fiscal.no_representation_grant` (off in production without an approved grant), `fiscal.gateway_not_enrolled` (off in production without the signed secure connection). On success the SaaS is told the new route at once.

POST /api/entitlement/refresh.name: Hand the hub its new entitlement (called by the SaaS)
POST /api/entitlement/refresh.description: What the SaaS calls after a plan change (hub#2105, saas#1959): the body carries the RS256 token of `GET /api/v1/hub/device/entitlement/` and the hub applies it at once, without a restart or closing sessions. No session or key: the signature is the authentication. `200 {"ok": true}` only when applied; `401 entitlement_token_invalid`, `403 entitlement_wrong_hub`, `409 entitlement_stale`, `429 entitlement_push_throttled` otherwise.
